learn.rule: A summary is one sentence with who or what and the most important thing.
learn.ruleEs: Un resumen es una oración con quién o qué y lo más importante.
learn.model: Ants build nests underground and store food in them.
learn.notice: A summary is short. It leaves out tiny details.

items.prompt: Which one is the best summary of the bee text?
items.text: Bees live in a hive. Worker bees find flowers. They bring nectar back to the hive. The nectar turns into honey.

options.text: Bees live in a hive.
Worker bees bring nectar to the hive to make honey.
Bees are small and yellow.

items.why: The best summary tells who (worker bees) and the big idea (making honey).
items.whyEs: El mejor resumen dice quién (worker bees) y la idea principal (hacer miel).

items.prompt: Check the tiny details we should cut from a bee summary.

options.text: Bees are yellow and black.
The hive is in an old tree.
Worker bees bring nectar to make honey.
Bees like warm days.

items.why: Colors and homes are tiny details. The summary keeps the big idea.
items.whyEs: Los colores y las casas son detalles pequeños. El resumen conserva la idea principal.

items.prompt: Which bee summary is too short?

options.text: Bees.
Worker bees make honey from nectar.
Bees live in a hive and are yellow and some have stripes and they fly.

items.why: A summary needs a who and the most important thing. Bees alone is too short.
items.whyEs: Un resumen necesita un quién y lo más importante. Solo Bees es muy corto.

items.prompt: Which bee summary is too long?

options.text: Bees make honey.
Bees live in a hive, and worker bees find flowers, and they bring nectar back, and it turns into honey.
Worker bees make honey from nectar.

items.why: A summary is one short sentence. The long one tells too many small things.
items.whyEs: Un resumen es una oración corta. La larga cuenta demasiadas cosas pequeñas.

items.model: Worker bees bring nectar to the hive to make honey.
items.why: Bring nectar to the hive is the most important thing the text says.
items.whyEs: Bring nectar to the hive es lo más importante que dice el texto.

items.prompt: Which bee summary has the wrong focus?

options.text: Worker bees bring nectar to make honey.
Bees have six legs.
Bees use nectar to make honey.

items.why: Six legs is not the big idea of the text.
items.whyEs: Las seis patas no son la idea principal del texto.

write.prompt: Say one sentence that tells the most important thing about this text.
write.promptEs: Di una oración que cuente lo más importante de este texto.
write.text: Frogs lay eggs in water. The eggs hatch into tadpoles. Tadpoles grow legs. Then they become frogs.

label: I said the most important thing
Dije lo más importante

write.model: A frog grows from an egg to a tadpole to a frog.

familyTalk.en: After a short story, tell the whole story in one sentence together.
familyTalk.es: Después de un cuento corto, cuenten todo el cuento en una oración juntos.

teacherTip.en: Read the text twice. Ask 'Who is it about?' and 'What is the most important thing?' before children choose.
teacherTip.es: Lee el texto dos veces. Pregunta '¿De quién trata?' y '¿Qué es lo más importante?' antes de elegir.

learn.rule: A summary is one sentence with who or what and the most important thing.
learn.ruleEs: Un resumen es una oración con quién o qué y lo más importante.
learn.model: Farmers grow food and sell it to people in town.
learn.notice: Keep the big idea. Cut tiny details.

items.prompt: Which one is the best summary of the library text?
items.text: A town needs a library. Many people borrow books there. Children come for story time. The library helps everyone learn.

options.text: The library has a front door.
Children like story time.
The library helps people learn by sharing books.

items.why: The best summary tells what the library does for everyone.
items.whyEs: El mejor resumen dice lo que hace la biblioteca por todos.

items.prompt: Check the tiny details we should cut from a library summary.

options.text: The library has a tall clock.
The librarian wears a green sweater.
Many people borrow books.
The front steps are gray.

items.why: Clocks, sweaters, and steps are tiny details.
items.whyEs: Los relojes, los suéteres y los escalones son detalles pequeños.

items.prompt: Which library summary is too short?

options.text: Library.
The library helps people learn.
The library has books and chairs and a desk and a clock.

items.why: One word does not tell who or what and the important thing.
items.whyEs: Una palabra no dice quién o qué ni lo importante.

items.prompt: Which library summary is too long?

options.text: The library lends books.
The library lends books, and children come for story time, and there are chairs and shelves and many people.
The library helps people learn.

items.why: The long one packs in too many small ideas.
items.whyEs: La oración larga junta demasiadas ideas pequeñas.

items.model: The library helps people learn by sharing books.
items.why: Helps people learn is the big idea of the text.
items.whyEs: Helps people learn es la idea principal del texto.

items.prompt: Which library summary has the wrong focus?

options.text: The library has a green door.
The library lends books to help people learn.
People borrow books at the library.

items.why: A green door is a tiny detail, not the main idea.
items.whyEs: Una puerta verde es un detalle pequeño, no la idea principal.

write.prompt: Say one sentence that tells the most important thing about this text.
write.promptEs: Di una oración que cuente lo más importante de este texto.
write.text: Mail carriers bring letters to homes. They walk or drive on their routes. They bring packages too. Mail carriers connect people.

label: I said the most important thing
Dije lo más importante

write.model: Mail carriers bring letters and packages to homes.

familyTalk.en: Tell your family about a helper in one sentence: who they are and what they do.
familyTalk.es: Cuenten a su familia sobre un ayudante en una oración: quién es y qué hace.

teacherTip.en: Have children hold up one finger for the one sentence a summary needs. Cut tiny details together.
teacherTip.es: Pide que levanten un dedo para la única oración que necesita un resumen. Eliminen juntos los detalles pequeños.

learn.rule: A summary is one sentence with who or what and the most important thing.
learn.ruleEs: Un resumen es una oración con quién o qué y lo más importante.
learn.model: Coins and bills are money that people use to buy things.
learn.notice: A summary names the topic and the big idea.

items.prompt: Which one is the best summary of the shape text?
items.text: A circle is round. A square has four equal sides. A triangle has three sides. Shapes are all around us.

options.text: A circle is round.
Shapes like circles, squares, and triangles are all around us.
A triangle has three sides.

items.why: The best summary names all the shapes and the big idea.
items.whyEs: El mejor resumen nombra todas las figuras y la idea principal.

items.prompt: Check the tiny details we should cut from a shape summary.

options.text: The square on my desk is blue.
Shapes are all around us.
My shoe box is brown.
Circles, squares, and triangles are shapes.

items.why: Colors of one object are tiny details.
items.whyEs: Los colores de un objeto son detalles pequeños.

items.prompt: Which shape summary is too short?

options.text: Shapes.
There are shapes all around us.
Shapes are round and square and have sides and corners and some are big.

items.why: One word is too short. A summary needs the big idea.
items.whyEs: Una palabra es muy corta. Un resumen necesita la idea principal.

items.prompt: Which shape summary is too long?

options.text: Shapes are all around us.
A circle is round, and a square has four sides, and a triangle has three sides, and shapes are all around.
Circles, squares, and triangles are shapes.

items.why: The long one repeats each shape detail instead of the big idea.
items.whyEs: La oración larga repite cada detalle en vez de la idea principal.

items.model: Circles, squares, and triangles are shapes all around us.
items.why: Are shapes all around us is the big idea of the text.
items.whyEs: Are shapes all around us es la idea principal del texto.

items.prompt: Which shape summary has the wrong focus?

options.text: Shapes are all around us.
A square has four equal sides.
Circles, squares, and triangles are all around us.

items.why: One shape detail is not the whole big idea.
items.whyEs: El detalle de una figura no es toda la idea principal.

write.prompt: Say one sentence that tells the most important thing about this text.
write.promptEs: Di una oración que cuente lo más importante de este texto.
write.text: Coins are small and round. People use coins to buy things. Some coins are worth more. Coins can be saved in a jar.

label: I said the most important thing
Dije lo más importante

write.model: People use coins to buy things.

familyTalk.en: Look at a short book page together and tell what it is about in one sentence.
familyTalk.es: Miren juntos una página de un libro corto y digan de qué trata en una oración.

teacherTip.en: Show the text. Ask children to point to the most important idea before they say their one sentence.
teacherTip.es: Muestra el texto. Pide que señalen la idea más importante antes de decir su oración.
